title: RACI and Cross-Functional Communication Basics
description: Learn how to use RACI matrices, working agreements, and async communication to align cross-functional teams.

interactions.prompt: In a RACI matrix, which role has final sign-off authority on a deliverable?

options.text: Responsible — the person doing the work
Accountable — the person who approves the outcome
Consulted — the subject matter expert giving input
Informed — the person notified after completion

interactions.teachingPreamble: A RACI matrix clarifies roles on cross-functional projects by assigning each person as Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, or Informed. For example, when Spotify launches a new feature, the product manager is typically Accountable (final sign-off), while engineers are Responsible (doing the build). Mixing these up is one of the top causes of project delays.

interactions.prompt: A project RACI shows 4 people marked 'Accountable' for the same deliverable, 2 marked 'Responsible,' and 0 'Consulted.' The project is 3 weeks behind schedule. What's the most likely root cause?

options.text: Too few people are doing the actual work
No subject matter experts were consulted
Multiple Accountable owners created unclear decision authority
Not enough people were kept informed

interactions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a cross-functional working agreement?

options.text: To legally bind teams to project deadlines
To set shared norms for communication, decisions, and escalation
To replace the need for regular standup meetings
To assign blame when deliverables are missed

interactions.teachingPreamble: Working agreements are lightweight team contracts that define how people collaborate — things like response times, meeting norms, and escalation paths. At Atlassian, cross-functional squads create working agreements at project kickoff, covering topics like 'Slack messages get a response within 4 hours during business hours.' These agreements reduce friction by making expectations explicit before conflicts arise.

interactions.prompt: In async communication best practices, a message should include context, the specific ____, and a clear deadline for response.

options.text: Ask or decision needed
Project budget update
Team member's job title
Meeting calendar invite

interactions.prompt: Your cross-functional team spans 3 time zones (New York, London, Tokyo). You need a weekly sync to unblock dependencies. Do you optimize for maximum live attendance or go fully async?

options.text: Rotate meeting times weekly so each timezone shares the burden
Pick the one overlapping hour and keep it consistent
Go fully async with a structured Slack/Loom update format
Hold two identical meetings so everyone attends a convenient one

interactions.prompt: Which standup format is best for surfacing cross-functional blockers quickly?

options.text: Each person gives a 5-minute detailed progress report
Focus on blockers first, then quick progress and plans
Only the project manager speaks and assigns tasks
Skip standups entirely and use a shared spreadsheet

interactions.teachingPreamble: Daily standups in cross-functional teams serve a different purpose than single-team standups — the goal is to surface dependencies and blockers between functions. At Shopify, cross-functional pods use a 'blockers-first' format: each person leads with what's stuck, then spends 15 seconds on progress. This keeps the meeting under 10 minutes and ensures the most critical alignment issues get airtime.

interactions.prompt: You're kicking off a new cross-functional project with Engineering, Design, Marketing, and Legal. Rank these alignment activities from what you should do first to last.

options.text: Set up a recurring standup cadence
Define the RACI for key deliverables
Create an async communication channel with norms
Draft a working agreement on decisions and escalations

interactions.prompt: Legal just flagged a compliance risk that requires sign-off before launch. No one on the RACI owns regulatory approval. Who should you escalate to, and what's your immediate action?

options.text: Ask the engineering lead to handle it since they own the build
Escalate to the Accountable person to update the RACI and assign ownership
Pause the entire project until Legal resolves the issue independently
Add everyone on the team as Consulted for compliance

interactions.priorContext: You had a clean RACI and working agreement in place, but a new compliance requirement surfaced mid-project that no existing role covers. The launch date is in 2 weeks.
